reviews: Paper-thin crust, fresh tomatoes and a pile of rocket on top. Feels light, and two slices cost less than a coffee and muffin.
Half the menu is veggie: roasted peppers, mushroom and spinach, grilled courgette. My meat-free friend had a hard time choosing.
Thin, crisp bases with fresh basil and a light hand on the cheese. Cheap and doesn't leave you sluggish for afternoon lectures.
Every single pizza comes topped with pepperoni, sausage or prosciutto, and they won't make one without. My vegetarian roommate had nothing to order.
Deep, doughy slices buried under three kinds of cheese, with grease pooling on the paper plate. Cheap and filling, but I needed a nap after.
Solid veggie slices if you skip the meat: the mushroom and pepper one is great. Just don't come here looking for anything light.
Still my favourite lunch cafe: fresh salads, grain bowls and a big pot of vegetable soup, all under ten bucks.
Sandwiches, soups and smoothies, no ovens for pizza here. Light, wholesome and lots of meat-free choices.
